text:
sam: heads-up — thinking about a compact audit sampling approach for automatic fallback triggers. current problem: full-audit for every fallback is too noisy and expensive.

sam: proposal sketch:
- keep a small always-on full-audit sample (0.5-1%) for forensic and regression detection
- maintain a larger compact-audit sample (10-20%) that captures metadata + hashes + short diffs
- for severe events (>=5xx spike or hallucination_score > 0.9) auto-escalate to full-audit for a short window

mira: love the tiers. quick q: what's in "compact" vs "full" specifically? also where does quota check live (routing vs billing)?

sam: compact = request/response hashes, model id/version, routing decision, latency buckets, error category, truncated output snippet (first 256 chars), user-decided tags. full = everything + full output + prompt text + raw tokens for eval teams.

kevin: re: quota, keep quota-handshake in the routing layer so decisions are synchronous. billing can consume the audit stream async but needs a marker that a request was decisioned due to quota/fallback.

jen: +1 to routing-handshake. also we need a unique fallback_id for tie-back across telemetry pipelines. otherwise joins across compact/full get messy.

sam: agreed. propose compact schema and sampling rules in config. quick draft config example:

```
fallback_audit:
  compact_sampling: 0.15
  full_sampling: 0.01
  escalation_on:
    - error_rate: {window: 60s, threshold: 0.05}
    - latency_p99_ms: 2500
    - hallucination_score: 0.9
  escalation_window: 300s
  attach_fallback_id: true
```

mira: can we add a quota_exempt flag so some legal/reg customers always get full-audit if they opt in? and a small TTL for full recordings to avoid storage blowup.

sam: yep add `full_preserve_days` and `opt_in_full_audit` flags. default TTL 7 days for full, 90 days for compact metadata. retention configs should be per-customer override only.

kevin: console needs to show sampling ratio and recent escalations per rollout. ops should be able to flip to 100% full-audit for a canary for a limited time. add a rate-limited toggle in console.

jen: UX thought: when an escalation happens, attach a short human-friendly reason in the audit event (e.g., "p99 latency 3.1s"). makes search and playbacks much faster.

mira: telemetry pipeline note: compact records should be lightweight newline-delimited JSON; full can be gzipped blobs. ensure we surface the same fallback_id in both so we can rehydrate.

sam: safety question: need to mask PII in compact samples? some customers may route private prompts. suggestion: default redact prompt and end-user message bodies in compact; full remains available only for opt-in and legal.

kevin: agreed. add `redact_level: none|partial|full` config per MSA. partial redaction: keep metadata + length + token count, remove messages.

opsbot: deploy-preview: rollout/fallback-audit v0.1 deployed to staging. See /deploys/rollouts/59812

jen: can we add a small simulation tool in console to run a historical trace through the sampling rules so PMs can see expected audit volume? makes quotas predictable.

sam: good idea. simulator outputs expected compact vs full counts and estimated storage. generate usage report per-day for billing teams.

mira: define an SLO for "audit attach success" (percentage of fallback events that produced at least compact audit). propose 99.5%.

kevin: +1. and a fallback_id TTL of 24h in the routing cache for joins across pipelines.

sam: next steps:
- draft telemetry schema + compact field set (sam)
- console toggle + simulator (jen)
- routing handshake + fallback_id propagation (kevin)
- retention/redaction policy + legal opt-in UX (mira)
I'll open individual tickets and a short RFC. any objections?

mira: none. looks good.

jen: no objections. will add console mocks after tickets.

kevin: no objections. will prototype the routing header.

opsbot: reminder: staging deploy will expire in 48h if no follow-up PRs.

sam: thanks all, i'll post RFC link when it's up :thumbsup:
